hero.headline: Uninterrupted Power for High-Density AI
hero.subheadline: Directly integrated with a captive power source, our facility eliminates grid instability and ensures a consistent 1MW flow to your hardware.

sections.title: Industrial-Grade Power Architecture
sections.body: The lifeblood of Kenya AI Compute is our proprietary power distribution network. Unlike traditional facilities that rely on aging national grids, we are connected via a dedicated, zero-distance high-voltage link to our captive hybrid power plant. This eliminates the risk of regional blackouts and provides a clean, stable sine wave required for the most sensitive H100 and A100 GPU clusters. Inside each modular unit, we deploy a sophisticated N+1 UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) architecture using high-density lithium-ion battery arrays. These systems act as a critical buffer, providing instantaneous failover while our secondary gas and diesel generation units synchronize. Every rack is serviced by redundant A+B power feeds, ensuring that even during scheduled maintenance of our primary generators, your computational tasks remain active and profitable.

items: Source: Direct captive hybrid generation (Solar + Gas) with industrial backup.

UPS System: N+1 modular lithium-ion UPS with >96% efficiency.
Monitoring: Per-outlet energy tracking via intelligent PDU units.
Surge Protection: Multi-stage TVSS protection throughout the electrical chain.

meta.title: Cooling & Thermal Management | Smart Airflow Design
meta.description: How we manage high-density heat loads. Direct expansion cooling, free cooling, and hot/cold aisle containment in Kenya.

hero.headline: Cooling the Minds of Machines
hero.subheadline: Our specialized cooling architecture is designed to handle 40kW racks while maintaining a target PUE of 1.3-1.5 in a tropical climate.

sections.title: Optimized Airflow for Maximum Performance
sections.body: Modern AI hardware operates at extreme thermal thresholds. A single GPU rack can generate as much heat as a small apartment building. To manage this, Kenya AI Compute utilizes a rigid Hot Aisle/Cold Aisle containment strategy within our modular units. By physically separating the chilled air from the heated exhaust, we eliminate air mixing and significantly reduce the workload on our precision cooling units (CRACs). We leverage Kenya's low-humidity climate to utilize air-side economizers, bringing in filtered outside air when temperatures are optimal. This 'Free Cooling' approach is the primary reason we can achieve a PUE (Power Usage Effectiveness) that rivals the best data centers in the world. For our 1MW Phase 2 expansion, we are also preparing liquid cooling loops for ultra-high density clusters, ensuring our facility remains future-proof as GPU wattages continue to rise.

sections.title: Thermal Control Systems
items: Containment: Rigid hot/cold aisle separation for 0% air bypass.
Economizers: Intelligent outside air usage to reduce compressor cycles.
Redundancy: N+1 cooling units per module to ensure continuous heat rejection.
Sensors: Real-time thermal mapping using thousands of IoT sensors.
Filtration: G4/F7 grade air filtration to prevent dust accumulation on GPUs.

hero.headline: The Neural Network of our Infrastructure

sections.title: Ultra-Low Latency Data Fabric
sections.body: Large-scale AI training is not just about the speed of individual GPUs; it is about the speed at which those GPUs can talk to each other. Kenya AI Compute has implemented a non-blocking Spine-Leaf network topology that provides predictable, low-latency communication between any two ports in our facility. Our core is 400G-ready, with 100G uplinks standard for every compute node. We utilize RDMA over Converged Ethernet (RoCE v2) to allow GPUs to share memory directly across the network, bypassing the CPU bottleneck. Externally, we maintain diverse fiber routes to the international cable landing stations in Mombasa. This multi-carrier strategy ensures that your AI APIs and DePIN nodes stay connected to the global internet with the lowest possible hop count to major IXPs in Europe and the Middle East.

sections.title: Multi-Layered Defense Strategy
sections.body: The security of our infrastructure is approached with zero-trust methodology. Physically, our site in Kenya is located within a gated industrial park with triple-redundant perimeter fencing and 24/7 armed security patrols. Access to individual compute modules requires multi-factor biometric authentication (fingerprint and iris scan) and is logged in real-time. Digitally, we protect the management network from the public internet using enterprise-grade firewalls and intrusion detection systems (IDS). For our DePIN and Cloud clients, we ensure complete logical isolation of traffic through advanced VLAN tagging and hardware-level encryption. Every server rack is equipped with vibration and door-opening sensors, instantly alerting our NOC (Network Operations Center) of any unauthorized physical proximity. In an era of increasing digital and physical threats, Kenya AI Compute provides a sanctuary for the world's most valuable computational assets.

sections.title: Balanced Infrastructure for a Global Market
sections.body: In building Kenya AI Compute, we avoided the trap of chasing 'vanity' top-tier GPUs that often come with low margins and long supply waits. Instead, we have engineered a hybrid server park designed for maximum utilization and rapid ROI. Our fleet is composed of 30% GPU nodes (focused on A100-class and modern AMD Instinct alternatives) for AI training and 3D rendering, and 50% high-core-count CPU nodes (AMD EPYC/Intel Xeon) for the massive demand in inference, edge computing, and decentralized cloud services. This 30/50/20 mix (GPU/CPU/Storage) ensures that we can fulfill the requirements of both the DePIN networks (like Render and Akash) and enterprise clients simultaneously. By utilizing high-performance but cost-effective hardware, we keep our CAPEX within the $14M-$18M range for the server park, allowing us to offer clients pricing that is 40% more affordable than global hyperscalers.

By operating within the Special Economic Zones (SEZ) framework, our project benefits from a world-class incentive package. This includes a reduced corporate income tax rate of just 10% for the first ten years of operation—a significant reduction from the standard 30% rate. Furthermore, the SEZ status grants us full exemption from Value Added Tax (VAT) on all project-related purchases and zero customs duties on imported high-tech equipment (servers, GPUs, cooling units). For international investors, the most critical benefit is the 0% withholding tax on dividends and interest payments remitted globally. This ensures a frictionless flow of capital and maximizes the cash yield for our equity partners, making Kenya one of the most fiscally attractive jurisdictions for infrastructure investment in the world.
